MANILA, Philippines – Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have opened a path to a possible “step-by-step” return of Myanmar’s political representatives to high-level meetings, although this remains conditional on Myanmar demonstrating concrete progress in implementing the bloc’s peace plan.

In their review and decision on the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus (5PC), ASEAN leaders agreed to pursue “calibrated engagement” with Myanmar through a “phased and progress-based approach.”

“Subject to sustained and concrete progress in the implementation of the 5PC by Myanmar, ASEAN may consider the gradual restoration of Myanmar’s full political representation,” said the document adopted on Sunday, November 15, the first day of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila.
In the same document, ASEAN leaders also reitered their “deep concern over the insufficient progress in the implementation of the 5PC.”

The regional bloc has previously left the door open for Myanmar’s political return. But the decision makes the possibility of a gradual restoration more explicit, even as leaders maintained existing restrictions.

In 2021, Myanmar’s military launched a coup that ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and plunged the country into a bloody civil war. Since then, ASEAN has barred Myanmar’s political leaders from attending ASEAN summits and foreign ministers’ meetings, allowing only non-political representatives to participate.

blocks.text: The decision comes amid calls from some member countries, particularly Thailand, to re-engage Myanmar’s military-backed government following elections held under military rule. The elections remain contentious, however, with ASEAN leaders only saying they “noted the conclusion of the three phases of Myanmar’s general elections,” without explicitly endorsing its validity.

Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro, who also serves as ASEAN’s special envoy on Myanmar, explained that the step-by-step approach would depend on whether Myanmar follows the peace plan.
“The step-by-step approach is adherence to the Five-Point Consensus. So, for example, the first one is cessation of hostilities,” Lazaro said in a press briefing on Sunday evening.

“We want to see how Myanmar responds to that because right now, there’s still certain bombings and displacement of Myanmar people. So step-by-step, we give it to them, how they’re going to tackle this issue, and we monitor that,” she added. – Rappler.com
